      "label":"Design-to-module evidence route"

      "definition":"Module-derived unit tests are module-owned proof lanes derived from module ownership evidence.       "key":"module_unit_proof",
      "label":"Module-derived unit proof"
    },
    {
      "conditions":["For every designed module, function, application surface, runtime surface, plugin surface, public interface, data surface, and published function or module of a profile."],
      "definition":"Lifecycle confirmation detects ambiguity about ultimate intended use at a realisation boundary. It consumes the operational lifecycle chain owned by SPEC_METHOD §2 without redefining its phases. It is neither a release plan nor a replacement for RELEASE.",
      "exceptions":[],
      "grounding":[{"end_line":1085,"quote":"The\ncanonical operational lifecycle chain is SPEC_METHOD §2 Operational\nlifecycle sufficiency; this section consumes that chain and does not\nredefine its phases. The checklist is not a release plan and does not\nreplace RELEASE; it is an ambiguity detector for ultimate intended use.","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md#ASSURANCE%2F16.%20Module%20lifecycle%20confirmation","start_line":1081}],
      "key":"module_lifecycle_confirmation",
      "label":"Module lifecycle confirmation"
    },
    {
      "conditions":[],
      "definition":"ASSURANCE's source ledger records received rc.2 SPEC_METHOD, STDO_REFERENCE_FRAME_BASELINE and DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD rows and their successor loci. Routes are provenance only; rows are asserted to be restated locally. Ticket test-case authority is routed to TICKETS §10. Profile terms are generalised: Ontology→ontology; IACS→declared carrier inventory; three-view evidence→domain/sequence/state evidence; co_evolution_admissible(B) and decision_complete(B)→design co-evolution condition and decision-complete; graph function or GTL module→published profile function/module; this method→design profile; agentic execution relation→ACTIVATION §1; RELEASE_METHOD→RELEASE. DESIGN_MODULE owns the object bindings. Predecessor must is rendered indicatively, while should, may and minimum retain force.",
      "exceptions":[],
      "grounding":[{"end_line":1146,"quote":"The predecessor's \"must\"\nis written in the indicative; \"should\", \"may\" and \"minimum\" keep their\nforce.","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md#ASSURANCE%2F17.%20Source%20dispositions","start_line":1144}],
      "key":"assurance_source_ledger",
      "label":"Assurance source-disposition ledger"
    },
    {
      "conditions":[],
      "definition":"The subject's Tier-1 AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS member owns the domain-specific, carrier-neutral STDO Axiomatic Calculus for Governed Symbolic Systems, a_c, with stable concept identity urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:a-c and bounded context urn:stdo:bounded-context:axiomatic-calculus. It owns position, signature, records, AC-001–AC-020, traversals, functor kinds, models, layers, identity, application boundaries, imports, exclusions and conformance. It consumes FOUNDATIONS ontology and core results without redefining them. These are descriptions of the subject calculus, not authority exercised by this interpretation.",
      "exceptions":[],
      "grounding":[
        {"end_line":12,"quote":"Consumes the ontology of\n[FOUNDATIONS §2](FOUNDATIONS.md) (subject, representation, interpretation,\ncontext, object, claim, evidence, judgment, authority, residual, basis,\nmaterial) and the core result algebra of\n[FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results); it states laws over\nthose objects and defines none of them a second time.","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS","start_line":7},
        {"end_line":29,"quote":"Its stable\nconcept identity is `urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:a-c`. This member\nowns that concept in the bounded context\n`urn:stdo:bounded-context:axiomatic-calculus`. Both identifiers are\ndeclared identities and do not change with the carrier or the directory\nthat publishes them (P3; rc.2 #position).","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F1.%20Position","start_line":24}
      ],
      "key":"subject_axiomatic_calculus",
      "label":"Subject a_c calculus"
    },
    {
      "conditions":[],
      "definition":"The derivation account identifies nine recurring commitment families and successor owners: scoped identity/authority conservation—FOUNDATIONS §2; bounded-context meaning/cross-context relations—FOUNDATIONS §2; bounded probabilistic construction—P0, FOUNDATIONS §2 and ACTIVATION §1; delegated construction, exact candidates and construction/assessment separation—ACTIVATION §1 and EVALUATION §3; ambiguity, human adjudication and hard stops—ACTIVATION §4; exact-basis evaluation, evidence/verdict separation and closed results—REFERENCE_FRAME RF-005/006/007 and FOUNDATIONS §4 restating RF-012; constitutional derivation/re-entry—SPEC_METHOD §1/§4; finite closure, projection, residuals and capability fit—REFERENCE_FRAME §3 and AC-010/011; singular released authority—SPEC_METHOD §6 and PRODUCT_DEFINITION at activation. Predecessor clause routes record derivation rather than application prerequisites.",
      "exceptions":[],
      "grounding":[{"end_line":70,"quote":"The calculus contracts recurring commitments the method already\nestablishes. In this corpus each is law in a member of this candidate, so\napplying the calculus needs no predecessor clause; the rc.2 clause family\nfrom which this edition derived each one is listed beside it as the\nderivation account that the identity record of §8 binds (P6; rc.2\n#derivation-provenance):","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F1.%20Position%2FDerivation%20provenance","start_line":65}],
      "key":"calculus_derivation_account",
      "label":"Calculus derivation account"
    },
    {
      "conditions":[],
      "definition":"Material family F9's foundation-to-law table distinguishes consequences from added choices and their owners. Its additional instance premises are: finite models represent governed symbolic systems; exact subjects, models and optional carriers are separately identified; some predicates are mechanical while others require bounded probabilistic construction or human adjudication. P1/P2/P3/P4a/P6 are marked independent, P0 recovered, P4b derived from P0/P2, and P5 derived from P0/P6. Added choices include calculus name/context/identity, eight record kinds and shapes, signature domains/kinds, composite-basis relations, refusal-cause precedence, latitude/disposition ownership, closure seeds/relation families, overlay/transformation ownership, functor permissions/application topology, interpretation and decision contracts, Product status, identity canonicalisation and issuance, application imports, projection checking contracts, and minimum conformance coverage. The table and consumer list explain dependency and ownership without deciding beyond owning rules.",
      "exceptions":[],
      "grounding":[{"end_line":161,"quote":"Instance premises,\nwhich the commitments do not supply:\n\n- (i) a governed symbolic system is represented by a finite model whose\n  records stand for its objects, relations, constraints, residuals,\n  traversals, transformations and judgments;\n- (ii) a model is interpreted from an exact subject and may be encoded in\n  a carrier, and subject, model and carrier are separately identified;\n- (iii) some predicates over a model are decided mechanically, and others\n  need bounded probabilistic construction or explicit human adjudication.","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F1.%20Position%2FFoundation%20to%20law","start_line":152}],
      "key":"foundation_law_map",
      "label":"F9 foundation-to-law and consumer map"
    },
    {
      "conditions":[],
      "definition":"Sigma=(RecordKind, Sort, RelationKind, ConstraintKind, ResidualKind, FunctorKind, JudgmentKind, StopKind). Each member is a finite closed identity set for one model family. RecordKind_ac fixes eight identities under urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind: with suffixes semantic-object, typed-relation, constraint, latitude, residual, traversal, transformation and judgment. The signature defines every sort/family's fields and value domains, identity-field reference domains/cardinalities, relation endpoint sorts, constraint subject/predicate domains, residual subject/uncertainty/consequence/re-entry domains, judgment input/output/evidence/stop contracts, and allowed traversal functor kinds.",
      "exceptions":[],
      "grounding":[{"end_line":232,"quote":"Sigma = (\n  RecordKind,\n  Sort,\n  RelationKind,\n  ConstraintKind,\n  ResidualKind,\n  FunctorKind,\n  JudgmentKind,\n  StopKind\n)","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F2.%20Signature","start_line":223}],
      "key":"calculus_signature",
      "label":"Closed model-family signature"
    },
    {
      "conditions":[],
      "definition":"The abstract exact-basis model is M_b=(b,I,O,E,C,L,X,V,T,J). Population_M maps the eight core kinds respectively to finite semantic objects, directed relations, constitutional constraints, latitude, residuals, traversals, transformations and judgments. Local_M is their disjoint union; I=Local_M disjoint_union External_M. RefDomain_Sigma(record_kind,field) supplies cardinality, allowed local record kinds, semantic-object sorts, external target kinds and required basis relation.",
      "exceptions":[],
      "grounding":[{"end_line":306,"quote":"`Population_M` is a total function over `RecordKind_ac`. Every population\nis finite, every fundamental record belongs to exactly one population, and\nrecord identities are unique across their disjoint union.","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F2.%20Signature","start_line":296}],
      "key":"axiomatic_model",
      "label":"Exact-basis axiomatic model"
    },
    {
      "conditions":[],
      "definition":"SemanticObject has exactly id, sort, context, owner, scope, basis, value. id/sort/context/owner/basis are identities; scope is the closed governed domain; value is sort-defined carrier-neutral content or an exact-content reference. It carries FOUNDATIONS' Object, scoped identity through id/owner/sort, and boundary through scope.",
      "exceptions":[],
      "grounding":[{"end_line":365,"quote":"`id`, `sort`, `context`, `owner` and `basis` are identities. `scope` is\nthe closed governed domain. `value` is sort-defined carrier-neutral content\nor a reference to exact content. A semantic object is an Object of\nFOUNDATIONS §2 whose scoped identity is carried by `id`, `owner` and\n`sort` and whose boundary is `scope`.","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F3.%20Typed%20records%2FSemantic%20object","start_line":361}],
      "key":"semantic_object_record",
      "label":"SemanticObject record"
    },
    {
      "conditions":[],
      "definition":"TypedRelation has exactly id, kind, source, target, context, owner, scope, basis, qualifiers. Endpoints resolve into I. qualifiers is a closed kind-specific record containing signature-required direction, cardinality, preservation, loss, inverse, invalidation or other semantics.",
      "exceptions":[],
      "grounding":[{"end_line":388,"quote":"`source` and `target` resolve to members of `I`. `qualifiers` is the\nclosed kind-specific record declaring direction, cardinality,\npreservation, loss, inverse, invalidation or other relation semantics\nrequired by the signature.","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F3.%20Typed%20records%2FTyped%20relation","start_line":385}],
      "key":"typed_relation_record",
      "label":"TypedRelation record"
    },
    {
      "conditions":[],
      "definition":"Constraint has exactly id, kind, applies_to, predicate, context, owner, scope, basis, judgment_kind, latitude_ref, refusal. kind resolves one declared ConstraintKind and judgment_kind one declared JudgmentKind. The signature owns predicate language and judgment semantics; a non-deterministically-decidable predicate states its required probabilistic or human judgment kind instead of claiming machine proof.",
      "exceptions":[],
      "grounding":[{"end_line":414,"quote":"`kind` resolves one declared `ConstraintKind`; `judgment_kind` resolves\none declared `JudgmentKind`. The owning signature defines the predicate\nlanguage and how its result is judged. A predicate that is not\ndeterministically decidable states the required probabilistic or human\njudgment kind rather than pretending to be a machine proof (P6, P1).","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F3.%20Typed%20records%2FConstraint","start_line":410}],
      "key":"constraint_record",
      "label":"Constraint record"
    },
    {
      "conditions":[],
      "definition":"Latitude is an explicit permission set inside a constraint boundary, with fields id, applies_to, allowed_variation, forbidden_variation, context, owner, scope, basis, invalidation. Silence grants no latitude, and permission cannot exceed owner, scope, basis or invalidation law.",
      "exceptions":[],
      "grounding":[{"end_line":438,"quote":"Silence is not latitude. Latitude grants no authority beyond its owner,\nscope, basis and invalidation law, an instance of\n[FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds), What\ncreates no authority (P6).","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F3.%20Typed%20records%2FLatitude","start_line":435}],
      "key":"latitude_record",
      "label":"Latitude record"
    },
    {
      "conditions":[],
      "definition":"Residual is first-class uncertainty content with fields id, subject, kind, uncertainty, consequence, context, owner, scope, basis, re_entry, invalidation. It carries FOUNDATIONS' Residual. kind resolves one declared ResidualKind; the signature defines lawful subject, uncertainty, consequence, re-entry and invalidation domains. Undeclared kinds or values refuse structural admission.",
      "exceptions":[],
      "grounding":[{"end_line":469,"quote":"`kind` resolves one declared `ResidualKind`. The owning signature defines\nits lawful subject, uncertainty, consequence, re-entry and invalidation\ndomains. An undeclared residual kind or value refuses structural admission\n(P3).","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F3.%20Typed%20records%2FResidual","start_line":466}],
      "key":"residual_record",
      "label":"Residual record"
    },
    {
      "conditions":["M, seed set Z and exact dependency relation family R are supplied."],
      "definition":"Material closure is closure_R(M,Z)=lfp(lambda Q: Z union required_R(M,Q)), the least lawful record closure under R. It makes no claim to globally minimal prose, bytes, tokens, cost or cognitive effort.",
      "exceptions":[],
      "grounding":[{"end_line":671,"quote":"Least\nclosure means least lawful record closure under `R`; it does not claim\nglobally minimal prose, bytes, tokens, cost or cognitive effort.","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F4.%20Fundamental%20laws%2FAC-010%20Material%20closure","start_line":669}],
      "key":"material_closure",
      "label":"Material closure"
    },
    {
      "conditions":[],
      "definition":"project(M,Z,R) returns (M_Z,Boundary_Z), gap or refusal. A projection selects a view without changing selected meaning; M_Z contains material closure, and Boundary_Z records excluded, external, unresolved, translated and invalidation-sensitive seams. It is a reference, not a new semantic owner. ACTIVATION §2 applies it to step context, and every projected corpus frame is such a projection.",
      "exceptions":[],
      "grounding":[{"end_line":688,"quote":"`M_Z` contains the material closure of `Z`, so a projection's `gap` or\n`refusal` is that of the closure it contains or of the model it acts on:\n`gap` or `refusal(basis)` (AC-007). `Boundary_Z` records excluded,\nexternal, unresolved, translated and invalidation-sensitive seams. A\nprojection is not a new semantic owner.","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F4.%20Fundamental%20laws%2FAC-011%20Projection","start_line":684}],
      "key":"model_projection",
      "label":"Model projection"
    },
    {
      "conditions":[],
      "definition":"A transformation specialises one exact traversal and bears an operation. Its record fields are id, traversal, domain_model, codomain_model, context, owner, scope, basis, operation_authority, preconditions, preservation_relation, preserved, introduced, removed, external_preserved, external_introduced, external_removed, external_resolution_witnesses, residuals, evidence, provenance, stop_states, invalidation, re_entry. T[t](M_b,inputs) returns proposed successor M_b_prime*, hold, gap or refusal; this description does not instantiate or apply a transformation.",
      "exceptions":[],
      "grounding":[{"end_line":709,"quote":"A transformation is an operation-bearing specialisation of one exact\ntraversal record `v` (§5). Its record is (P4b, P3; rc.2\n#ac-013-transformation):","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F4.%20Fundamental%20laws%2FAC-013%20Transformation","start_line":707}],
      "key":"transformation_record",
      "label":"Transformation contract"
    },
    {
      "conditions":[],
      "definition":"A judgment is a model record pointing to an unchanged subject, with fields id, kind, subject, subject_digest, context, owner, scope, basis, evaluator, authority, decision, evidence, provenance, decided_at. This describes the record kind and issues no judgment.",
      "exceptions":[],
      "grounding":[{"end_line":896,"quote":"A judgment points to an unchanged subject; it is the Judgment of\nFOUNDATIONS §2 carried as a model record (P6; rc.2\n#ac-014-judgment-separation):","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F4.%20Fundamental%20laws%2FAC-014%20Judgment%20separation","start_line":894}],
      "key":"judgment_record",
      "label":"Judgment record"
    },
    {
      "conditions":[],
      "definition":"A traversal is a typed contract v with fields id, domain, codomain, context, owner, scope, basis, preconditions, postconditions, authority, evidence, provenance, stop_states. F_K[v](X_v) returns typed result Y_v or a value of closed stop algebra Omega_v. Same-spelled runtime/profile/realisation terms neither import nor specialise this concept without an owner-authorised declared binding.",
      "exceptions":[],
      "grounding":[{"end_line":947,"quote":"The traversal record is this member's own concept. A same-spelled term\nowned by a profile, a realisation or a runtime is not imported by nominal\nequality and does not specialise this record except through a declared\nbinding under that owner's authority (§9; P3, P1).","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F5.%20Traversals%20and%20functor%20kinds","start_line":944}],
      "key":"traversal_contract",
      "label":"Traversal contract"
    },
    {
      "conditions":[],
      "definition":"Three generic functor kinds have identities urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-d, :f-p and :f-h. F_D classifies deterministic evaluation/proof of declared properties, returns a judgment and does not perform judged domain construction. F_P classifies bounded probabilistic interpretation, construction or proposal under an exact contract; usefulness or repeatability confers no semantic, admission, acceptance or closure authority. F_H classifies explicit human adjudication under exact identity, grant, subject, basis and decision contract; human presence confers no ambient authority. Actor, executor, domain operation and kind are distinct; Encode/Interpret/Serialize/Measure are not kind aliases. Shared kind does not imply shared traversal identity or semantics. The name asserts no categorical functor; categorical claims require the FOUNDATIONS Formal fragment demonstration.",
      "exceptions":[],
      "grounding":[{"end_line":997,"quote":"- `F_D` classifies deterministic evaluation or proof over declared\n  properties. It returns a judgment and does not perform the domain\n  construction being judged (P6).\n- `F_P` classifies bounded probabilistic interpretation, construction or\n  proposal under an exact traversal contract. Its result has no semantic,\n  admission, acceptance or closure authority merely because it is useful\n  or repeatable (P6, P0; instance premise (iii) of §1 Foundation to law).\n- `F_H` classifies explicit human adjudication under an exact identity,\n  authority grant, subject, basis and decision contract. Human presence\n  grants no ambient authority (P6).","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F5.%20Traversals%20and%20functor%20kinds","start_line":988}],
      "key":"generic_functor_kinds",
      "label":"F_D, F_P and F_H"
    },
    {
      "conditions":[],
      "definition":"Interpret_a_c(subject_basis,signature,interpretation_contract) returns proposed model M_subject*, hold, gap or refusal. The star denotes absence of applicable semantic acceptance. The contract declares exact calculus basis; exact subject identity, inventory, bytes or semantic addresses; signature and compatible extension; mappings to all applicable populations; interpreter identity/capability/provenance/stops; structural evaluation contract; semantic selection/acceptance authority; source re-entry and invalidation rules. Stops map by cause under AC-007.",
      "exceptions":[],
      "grounding":[{"end_line":1055,"quote":"The stops `hold`, `gap` and `refusal` take their core values under AC-007\nby their causes. The trailing `*` marks a proposed model that has not\nreceived the\napplicable semantic acceptance judgment. The interpretation contract is\nthe Interpretation of FOUNDATIONS §2 made exact for one subject and one\nsignature.","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F6.%20Interpretation%20and%20models","start_line":1050}],
      "key":"subject_interpretation",
      "label":"Exact-subject interpretation"
    },
    {
      "conditions":[],
      "definition":"The three layers are a_c (pure calculus), a_c.X (subject X interpreted as a model), and a_c.X.C (accepted model encoded in carrier C). M_X=Interpret_a_c(X); J_X=Accept_X(M_X) yields accepted or refuse; Encode_C(M_X,J_X) requires accepted; deterministic F_D[v_carrier_admission] judges G_C against Profile_C and CarrierBasis_C and yields admitted or refuse. The admitted encoding evidence is (G_C,J_X,D_C).",
      "exceptions":[],
      "grounding":[{"end_line":1133,"quote":"M_X = Interpret_a_c(X)\nJ_X = Accept_X(M_X) -> accepted | refuse\nG_C = Encode_C(M_X, J_X) where J_X = accepted\nD_C = F_D[v_carrier_admission](G_C, Profile_C, CarrierBasis_C)\n      -> admitted | refuse","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-generation-rc9/claude/c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F7.%20Layers","start_line":1129}],
      "key":"governed_calculus_layers",
      "label":"Calculus, interpreted-model and encoded-carrier layers"
    },
